topic: Sentence-level citation grounding for long-document question answering

selected_papers.title: SpanCite: Sentence-Level Citation Grounding for Long-Document QA
selected_papers.abstract: We propose SpanCite, a decoding-time constraint that requires each generated sentence to be traceable to a specific source span before it is emitted. On a long-document QA benchmark, SpanCite reduces the rate of unsupported claims in generated answers, at the cost of a small added latency overhead from the constrained decoding step. All experiments use English-language documents.

executive_summary.content: This review covers SpanCite, a method that constrains generation so each sentence in a long-document answer stays traceable to a specific source passage.

introduction_scope.content: Retrieval-augmented generation systems sometimes produce sentences that are not actually backed by any retrieved passage. This review covers exactly one paper on this problem, SpanCite, and does not attempt a broader survey of grounding methods.

thematic_findings.content: SpanCite's central contribution is a decoding-time constraint that ties each generated sentence to a source span before it is emitted [1].

methodology_landscape.content: SpanCite works by checking, at each sentence boundary during decoding, whether a candidate sentence can be traced to a specific span in the retrieved documents; sentences that fail this check are regenerated [1].

contradictions_open_debates.content: As the only paper in this review, SpanCite has no other method to be compared against or contradicted by.

gap_analysis.content: SpanCite's evaluation is limited to English-language documents, and the paper does not report how much the constrained decoding step slows generation in absolute terms [1].

future_research_directions.content: A natural next step is testing SpanCite's constraint on non-English documents, since its current evaluation is English-only [1].

conclusion.content: SpanCite eliminates all unsupported claims in long-document question answering [1].

refinement_context.notes: Draft's Conclusion overclaims that SpanCite 'eliminates all' unsupported claims; SpanCite's own abstract only reports a reduction in the rate of unsupported claims. Refined corrects the claim using the same evidence and the same citation -- a clean, isolated groundedness fix with no other section touched.
refinement_context.adjudication_note: R6D.3b (2026-08-11): after run_id 5's calibrated live pass (commit acab474) predicted analytical_quality/template_fit/coherence improved (this fixture originally expected all three unchanged), a human reviewer re-read the frozen R6C rubric definitions for those three dimensions against the actual draft/refined Conclusion text and determined the predicted directions were each independently defensible under the EXISTING, unmodified rubric -- not a case of relaxing the rubric or blindly copying the judge's output. This was human adjudication against a frozen definition, never an automatic 'match whatever the judge said' correction: the original expectations were too artificially isolated, treating a Conclusion-only edit as incapable of touching any dimension beyond citation_correctness/groundedness, when the frozen definitions for analytical_quality (conclusions following evidence), template_fit (evidence-grounded Foundational framing), and coherence (logical alignment across sections) all genuinely bear on the same one-sentence fix.

citation_correctness.rationale: The draft's Conclusion claim ('SpanCite eliminates all unsupported claims') is a superlative its one attached source does not establish, so under r6c2-citation-aggregation-v2 that source's per-claim verdict is does_not_support -- a real citation defect. The refined Conclusion ('SpanCite reduces the rate of unsupported claims') is exactly what the same source states, so the same source's per-claim verdict becomes supports. This is a fail-to-pass transition on the one claim unit that actually changed, under R6D.3a's changed-claim-only citation_correctness derivation -- a genuine improvement, not a wash.

groundedness.rationale: The draft's Conclusion claims SpanCite 'eliminates all' unsupported claims; SpanCite's abstract reports only a reduction in the rate of unsupported claims, a materially narrower finding. The refined Conclusion restates the same finding accurately, using the same evidence and citation, with nothing new added.

synthesis_quality.rationale: This is a single-paper review in both versions; no cross-source synthesis claim is made either way, so there is nothing for this dimension to move on.

analytical_quality.rationale: R6D.3b human adjudication against the frozen analytical_quality definition (judges/holistic.py's own rubric: 'do conclusions follow from the cited evidence rather than overreaching'): correcting the unsupported absolute conclusion makes the report's conclusion follow the supplied evidence rather than overreaching, which is explicitly part of that frozen definition -- Gap Analysis and Future Research Directions being byte-identical does not exhaust this dimension's own scope.

template_fit.rationale: R6D.3b human adjudication against the frozen template_fit definition: the Foundational template's own expectation requires evidence-grounded framing rather than padded, unsupported claims. Replacing an absolute unsupported guarantee ('eliminates all') with the source-bounded finding ('reduces the rate of') improves that fit without changing reader depth, introducing new terminology, or adding padding.

coherence.rationale: R6D.3c rubric-boundary clarification (not automatic label copying): the correction improves factual support and analytical precision, but does not change document flow, structure, repetition, transitions, or resolve an explicit contradiction between report sections; those other improvements are already captured by citation_correctness, groundedness, analytical_quality, and template_fit. Run 5 (coherence=improved, confidence=0.72) and run 6 (coherence=unchanged, confidence=0.98) disagreed on exactly this boundary; run 6's higher-confidence result and this rubric re-read both point to unchanged.

source_balance.rationale: The single source is cited the same number of times, in the same sections, in both versions.
